datasets.title: Luxembourg housing asking prices by commune and month
datasets.description: Asking prices per square metre of living area for apartments and houses offered for sale or rent in each of Luxembourg's 100 communes and in the 24 official quarters of Luxembourg City. Values are the median and the 25th and 75th percentiles of the residential listings that were active on ChatHome when the statistics were computed; ChatHome collects these listings from estate-agency websites. The data has four segments (sale apartment, sale house, rent apartment, rent house), a current snapshot per commune and per quarter, and a monthly history in long format that grows with each release. A median or quartile is published only when at least 5 listings support it; otherwise the cell is empty, never zero. With few listings, a median or quartile can equal a single advert's asking price per m²; the adverts are public, so this reveals no private data. For reference, the commune snapshot also carries, where available, two official Observatoire de l'Habitat series from data.public.lu: the mean asking rent over a rolling 12-month window and the mean registered apartment sale price. These differ from the ChatHome figures in statistic (mean, not median), window, source and coverage, and the registered price is a transaction figure while every other price here is an asking price. Each commune row carries the official 4-digit commune code used by STATEC and data.public.lu.

warnings: Upstream source accuracy is not certified. A separate 24-page current-active spot-check found a legacy energy-class conflict and an active record whose retained description says sold. Exact membership of these adverts in this dated export is unverified; these findings do not measure the export error rate. No raw source facts were repaired or invented for this release.
Publishable commune medians: sale_apartment 81/100; sale_house 97/100; rent_apartment 24/100; rent_house 3/100. These are advert samples, not unique dwellings or the whole market.
History contains 2026-07, 2026-08, 2026-10; missing months are absent. Different source methods and stock composition prevent interpreting this as a quality-adjusted index.

datasets.title: Advertised homes and asking prices by energy class, Luxembourg and border regions
datasets.description: How the homes advertised for sale and for rent in Luxembourg and in the neighbouring areas of France, Belgium (Wallonia) and Germany are distributed across energy-performance classes, and what they ask per square metre in each class. Each country keeps its own certificate scheme and headline indicator: the Luxembourg CPE primary-energy class (A+ to I), the French DPE energy-consumption class (A to G), the Walloon PEB class (A++ to G) and the German Energieausweis class (A+ to H). Letters are never pooled or converted across schemes. A listing whose class is missing, on another axis or outside its scheme's scale counts as not stated, and not-stated rows are published so the gap stays visible. The source is a one-day snapshot of the public ChatHome catalogue of active listings, which ChatHome collects from estate-agency websites. Counts and shares need at least 5 listings, because smaller counts are unreliable; the adverts are public and this is not a confidentiality guarantee, as a hidden count can sometimes be worked out from the shares. Median, 25th and 75th percentile asking prices per m² and new-build shares need at least 10. A second table gives the class mix by Luxembourg canton. The shares describe advertised stock on the snapshot date. They are not the national certificate registers and not the housing stock.

warnings: Upstream source accuracy is not certified. A separate 24-page current-active spot-check found a legacy energy-class conflict and an active record whose retained description says sold. Exact membership of these adverts in this dated export is unverified; these findings do not measure the export error rate. No raw source facts were repaired or invented for this release.

Price differences between CPE classes are unadjusted associations, not a causal energy premium or renovation return. Missing certificate labels and new-build/location composition can change the result.
LU sale CPE not stated: apartment 31.9%; house 43.1%. Unknown subsidy values remain empty.

tables.name: energy_class_asking_prices
tables.title: Advertised homes and asking prices by energy class
tables.description: Apartments (studios included) and houses advertised for sale or rent on the snapshot date, by country, tenure, property type and energy-performance class, with each class's share and its asking price per m². The class is the one each country's certificate states on its headline scale: Luxembourg CPE primary energy, French DPE energy consumption, Walloon PEB overall performance, German Energieausweis overall performance. Values on another indicator or off the scheme's scale count as not_stated. Letters are not comparable across countries. Rooms, colocations, multi-unit buildings and land are excluded. Price per m² is the asking price (or monthly base rent) divided by the living area, kept only for areas of 10–2,000 m², sale prices of 500–40,000 EUR/m² and rents of 3–120 EUR/m² a month; listings outside these bands still count in class shares, because their class is known, but not in price statistics. Asking prices are not transaction prices. Every class of the scale and not_stated is listed for each country, tenure and type with at least one listing, so absence is explicit.

datasets.title: Modelled travel times from Luxembourg and cross-border communes to six Luxembourg job hubs
datasets.description: Modelled door-to-door travel times from every Luxembourg commune and from the French and German communes where at least 100 residents work in Luxembourg (IGSS counts, at most 400 communes) to six Luxembourg destinations: Luxembourg station, Kirchberg, Cloche d'Or, the city centre, Belval and Findel airport. Each row gives one origin, destination and weekday scenario: driving off-peak and at the morning and evening peaks, public transport in the morning and evening peaks, walking and cycling. Road, walking and cycling times come from the open-source Valhalla router on OpenStreetMap; public-transport times come from the R5 router on official GTFS timetables, with the 80th percentile published next to the median. Peak driving times are modelled with a national congestion ratio, not measured traffic. A median over 120 minutes is reported as no journey found, never as zero.Every row states when its timetable or road graph stops being valid. Belgian communes are not included while the licence of their centroid source is unresolved. Because the times are derived from OpenStreetMap, the dataset is published under the ODbL.

licence.name: Open Data Commons Open Database License 1.0

warnings: Modelled journeys from a commune reference point are not measured door-to-door commutes. Centroid checks concern origin representativeness; missing journeys are not zero minutes.

tables.name: commune_hub_travel_times
tables.title: Commune-to-hub travel times
tables.description: Routed weekday travel times between each reference commune (every Luxembourg commune, and the French and German communes with at least 100 residents working in Luxembourg) and six Luxembourg employment hubs, in eight scenarios: driving off-peak and at peak in both directions, public transport in the morning and evening peaks, walking and cycling. Road, walking and cycling times come from a self-hosted Valhalla router on OpenStreetMap; public-transport times from a self-hosted R5 router on official GTFS timetables. Where no journey within the cutoff was found the status says so and the minutes are empty, never zero.

columns.description: Grande Région locality id: lu:lau:<code>, fr:insee:<code> or de:ags:<code>.

columns.name: country
columns.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the commune: LU, FR or DE.

columns.name: national_code
columns.description: Official municipality code: STATEC 4-digit, INSEE 5-digit or Destatis 8-digit AGS.

columns.name: hub_id
columns.description: Hub identifier, e.g. lux-gare or kirchberg.

columns.name: hub_name
columns.description: Hub name in English.

columns.name: scenario_id
columns.description: Scenario identifier, e.g. transit-weekday-am-to-target.

columns.name: mode
columns.description: driving, transit, walking or cycling.

columns.name: direction
columns.description: to_target (commune to hub) or from_target (hub to commune).

columns.name: time_basis
columns.description: depart_at, arrive_by, or static for time-invariant walking and cycling.

columns.name: window_from
columns.description: Start of the weekday local-time window (Europe/Luxembourg, HH:MM); empty for static modes.

columns.name: window_to
columns.description: End of the weekday local-time window (Europe/Luxembourg, HH:MM); empty for static modes.

columns.name: status
columns.description: ok; no_journey_within_cutoff: no journey within cutoff_minutes was found (a longer journey, a point the network does not reach, or for public transport too few departures in the window; the surface does not tell these apart); not_routed: the commune's centroid cell is not in the routing surface.

columns.name: minutes_p50
columns.description: Median journey time in minutes, 1 decimal; status ok only, so never above cutoff_minutes. Public transport: over the window minutes that have a journey within cutoff_minutes (at least 70% of them), including a per-ride reliability allowance calibrated on mobiliteit.lu observations.

columns.name: minutes_p80
columns.description: 80th-percentile journey time in minutes over the same window minutes as minutes_p50, with the per-ride allowance, 1 decimal; it can exceed cutoff_minutes. Public transport with status ok only, empty for driving, walking and cycling.

columns.name: distance_km
columns.description: Median routed distance in kilometres, 1 decimal; status ok only, empty for public transport.

columns.name: cutoff_minutes
columns.description: Longest journey the surface searched for.

columns.name: centroid_check

schema.name: Modelled travel times from Luxembourg and cross-border communes to six Luxembourg job hubs
schema.description: Modelled door-to-door travel times from every Luxembourg commune and from the French and German communes where at least 100 residents work in Luxembourg (IGSS counts, at most 400 communes) to six Luxembourg destinations: Luxembourg station, Kirchberg, Cloche d'Or, the city centre, Belval and Findel airport. Each row gives one origin, destination and weekday scenario: driving off-peak and at the morning and evening peaks, public transport in the morning and evening peaks, walking and cycling. Road, walking and cycling times come from the open-source Valhalla router on OpenStreetMap; public-transport times come from the R5 router on official GTFS timetables, with the 80th percentile published next to the median. Peak driving times are modelled with a national congestion ratio, not measured traffic. A median over 120 minutes is reported as no journey found, never as zero.Every row states when its timetable or road graph stops being valid. Belgian communes are not included while the licence of their centroid source is unresolved. Because the times are derived from OpenStreetMap, the dataset is published under the ODbL.
schema.citation: ChatHome (chathome.lu), Modelled travel times from Luxembourg and cross-border communes to six Luxembourg job hubs, 2026.10-5. https://chathome.lu/en/data
